newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen firms in subdued pre-summit trade.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen firms in subdued pre-summit trade.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen interest rate futures settled slightly higher on Thursday after Tokyo stocks erased part of their earlier gains by the close.

But activity was slim throughout the day ahead of the Group of Seven industrialised nations' summit this weekend in Denver and the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) key quarterly "tankan" corporate survey next week, traders said. The December was up 0.01 at 99.10 in turnover of a small 20,394 contracts.

"The market was lacklustre because of little movement in the stock and currency markets," said a trust bank dealer. "But it seems that the December may rise to and above 99.15 some time before the tankan is released (on June 25) because many expect the tankan to show worsening corporate sentiment."
The interest rate swap (IRS) market was also dull, giving no clue to the December. The three-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.49/1.53 percent against Wednesday's 1.50/1.54 percent.
But a city bank dealer said he saw a risk of higher interest rates.

"I'm growing cautious about betting the tankan will show weak results because the BOJ governor said yesterday that the recent strength in the yen seems to have had little impact on the sentiment of corporate managers," the dealer said.
In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate was mainly traded at around 0.51 percent, little changed from Wednesday's 0.52 percent.

The BOJ drained 200 billion yen from the money market, which had been in surplus of some 190 billion yen. It was the fourth day the bank had conducted a neutral operation since the current reserve reporting period started on Monday.
The impact of the neutral operation was limited although some had expected the BOJ to end such an operation this morning and take a more accommodative credit stance.
Traders said upward pressure in the short-end of the market was easing after banks raised a large sum of longer-term funds by issuing certificates of deposit (CDs) on Wednesday.

On Thursday, some 50 billion yen of key three-month CDs were issued at 0.60 percent. Some 100 billion yen of one-month CDs were issued at 0.58 percent, while around 50 billion yen of two-month CDs were issued at 0.59 percent. These rates were flat from Wednesday's levels.
